With a sensitive ear for the language of New York and a keen sense of what makes each of his characters unique, Guirgis has written a play that is as complex and wondrous as the world we inhabit.
Guirgis’ compassionate play, directed with great care by Austin Pendleton, is also wildly funny — actually more hilarious than many recent flat-out comedies — and devilishly inappropriate.

Everyone should see it anyway, to experience the pleasure of a great cast making a shrimps-and-veal meal of the incredibly rich material, even as it flips between comedy and tragedy on its way to the truth in between.

Between Riverside and Crazy is a play about gentrification, police brutality, and the American dream deferred, but it's also about the small moments of grace that can emerge from the most unlikely circumstances.
There are so many reasons to admire and respect—even love—Stephen Adly Guirgis' Between Riverside and Crazy that it's almost a challenge to know where to start.
Here is the perfect play, and one of the last Broadway openings of the year.

What makes ‘Between Riverside and Crazy’ resonate as more than a deliciously dark comedy is the compassion and wisdom that Stephen Adly Guirgis brings to its flawed characters, and to others who invite less sympathy.

As subtle in its craft as it is blunt in its language — and performed by a first-rate cast — the play is likely to make you delight in all the New Yorkers on stage in the first act…and then force you to question your initial judgement in the second.
There are some truly great performances on Broadway this season, but none is more impressive than Henderson’s turn in “Between Riverside and Crazy.”
The play could not be in better hands.
After a while, even his cantankerous comedy and silent currents of emotion can’t bring this dreary play north of a puzzled, heavy eye-lidded look.
His portrayal of the irascible, foul-mouthed, deeply stubborn – yet sometimes kind -
Walter “Pops” Washington, a deeply human portrayal of a contemporary Everyman, is the playwright’s towering achievement.
Line by line, Between Riverside and Crazy delivers as much pleasure as any play in New York right now.
